stem: A client with type 2 diabetes says that several traditional foods are central to family meals and worries that diabetes care will require giving them up completely. Which response by the nurse is best?

options.A: Work with the client and, when appropriate, a registered dietitian nutritionist to build an individualized eating plan that incorporates cultural food preferences while meeting metabolic and nutrition goals.
options.B: Advise the client to stop eating all traditional foods because culturally familiar eating patterns are incompatible with diabetes management.
options.C: Give the same standardized meal plan used for every client so cultural preferences do not influence diabetes education.
options.D: Avoid discussing food preferences because medical nutrition therapy should focus only on carbohydrate grams and not on the client’s usual eating pattern.

rationale: A is correct. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care state that there is no one-size-fits-all eating pattern for diabetes and recommend individualized medical nutrition therapy and meal planning based on current eating patterns, metabolic goals, personal and cultural preferences, access to food, and other person-specific factors. DSMES should also be culturally and socially appropriate. B, C, and D conflict with person-centered nutrition care and can create unnecessary barriers to sustainable self-management.
educational_objective: Provide culturally responsive diabetes nutrition education by incorporating the client’s usual foods and preferences into an individualized eating plan that supports metabolic and nutrition goals.
source_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee
source_document_title: Facilitating Positive Health Behaviors and Well-being to Improve Health Outcomes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
source_locator: Recommendation 5.5 — provide culturally and socially appropriate DSMES responsive to personal preferences and needs; Medical Nutrition Therapy and ‘Eating Patterns and Meal Planning’ — no one-size-fits-all eating pattern, individualized plans based on usual eating style, cultural background, preferences, metabolic goals, and social determinants; Recommendation 5.10 — individualized MNT by an RDN
source_claim_supported: Current ADA guidance recommends culturally responsive, individualized diabetes nutrition planning that incorporates usual eating patterns and personal/cultural preferences rather than requiring abandonment of traditional foods or use of a universal meal plan.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — provide individualized health education and nutrition-related self-management support that respects client values and preferences
blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — culturally responsive diabetes nutrition education
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source item into a person-centered client-teaching scenario and reclassified it from Management of Care to Health Promotion and Maintenance. The final version is directly grounded in ADA 2026 cultural-responsiveness and individualized nutrition recommendations rather than the vague phrase ‘diabetes-friendly principles.’
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified directly against ADA Standards of Care 2026 Section 5. The source explicitly requires culturally/socially appropriate DSMES and individualized eating plans based on cultural background and preferences.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A reflects current nutrition guidance and appropriate RDN collaboration without asserting that any specific traditional food is automatically healthy or unhealthy.
audit_findings.choice_A: Correct; it individualizes nutrition while respecting culture and metabolic goals.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; current guidance does not require abandonment of traditional foods.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; one standardized meal plan conflicts with individualized, person-centered care.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; usual eating patterns, preferences, and cultural background are specifically relevant to nutrition planning.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A integrates both cultural preferences and evidence-based individualized nutrition goals.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices address how to incorporate culture into nutrition counseling.
audit_findings.blueprint: Health Promotion and Maintenance is the best fit because the construct is preventive self-management nutrition education.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked cultural responsiveness versus stereotyping, individualized MNT, RDN referral scope, no-one-size-fits-all language, category mapping, and second-answer risk. No unresolved conflict remained.
